title: The oldest cluster in its cloud
caption: The globular cluster NGC 121, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 121 · constellation Tucana · about 200000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Hubble's subject here is NGC 121, a globular cluster seen in the direction of Tucana, the Toucan. These clusters are big balls of old stars that circle the centres of their galaxies like satellites. This one belongs not to the Milky Way but to one of our neighbours, the Small Magellanic Cloud.

Because NGC 121 lies relatively close, Hubble can pick out its individual stars and study them in detail. Old clusters like this act as markers that trace the wider population of stars in the galaxy they belong to, helping astronomers learn how stars there formed and evolved.

NGC 121 is around 10 billion years old, the oldest cluster in its galaxy, where the others are 8 billion years old or younger. Even so, it is still several billion years younger than comparable clusters in the Milky Way and the Large Magellanic Cloud. Why is not fully clear. Cluster formation may have been delayed in the Small Magellanic Cloud, or NGC 121 may be the lone survivor of an older group.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.68 x 2.62 arcminutes) and distance (200000 light years), the frame spans roughly 156 × 152 light-years. Its light set out about 200,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The image was taken with Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys through a visible and a near-infrared filter. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and Hubble's sharp vision resolves individual stars that an eye would see only as a hazy patch.

explore: English astronomer John Herschel discovered the cluster in 1835. The Milky Way has roughly 150 globular clusters. A version of this image was entered in the Hubble's Hidden Treasures image processing competition by Stefano Campani.
alt: A dense, rounded cluster of many individual stars.
